summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +18.5%; weakest: Oats -17.9%. Key releases ahead: US Advance GDP q/q (10-29 8:30 AM ET); US Core PCE Price Index m/m (10-29 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.05% (-19 bp in a month), 2-year 4.67% (-25 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (+6 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.00% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.28 (+0.9% in a month, +4.1% YTD). USD/BRL 5.349 (+2.4% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.651 (-0.9%); USD/MXN 18.75 (+4.3%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.8% in a month (+13.1% YTD); VIX 17.0. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 101.46 $/bbl (+16.3% in a month), Brent 110.50, ULSD 4.536 $/gal (+4.7%), natural gas 2.95 (-11.7%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -0.2% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.7%, Hang Seng -6.4%, yuan +0.9% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 13 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (39%); S&P GSCI +4.5% in a month; gold -3.5%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
